name: Chris DeWolfe

name: Mark Pincus

He worked at Lazard Freres for two years, then moved to Hong Kong as VP at Asian Capital Partners, before returning for an MBA at Harvard Business School (1993). His first startup, FreeLoader, launched in 1995.

name: Joshua Schachter
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Schachter created Memepool in the late 1990s and Muxway in 2001, but these were personal side projects; Delicious (del.icio.us) was not launched until September 2003 when he was 29, and he was working as an analyst at Morgan Stanley until March 2005.

He launched Delicious in September 2003 and began working on it full-time in March 2005.

name: Caterina Fake
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Fake graduated from Vassar College in 1991 and was in her post-college exploration period working various jobs (painter's assistant, investment banker, dive shop) around age 26 (1995); she did not learn web programming until 1994 and co-founded Flickr in 2004 at age 35.
early_history_summary: Fake was raised in northern New Jersey by her American father and Filipina mother. She graduated from Choate Rosemary Hall in 1986 and Vassar College in 1991 with a degree in English. After college she worked various jobs before landing in San Francisco, where she taught herself web programming and created websites and CD-ROMs. She joined Netscape in 1997 to manage community forums, then worked at Salon.com, before co-founding Ludicorp with Stewart Butterfield in 2002, which launched Flickr in 2004.
family_context_summary: Raised in northern New Jersey by an American father and Filipina mother. Not allowed to watch television as a child; hobbies included reading poetry and playing classical music. Family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.

name: Stewart Butterfield
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Butterfield earned his BA from the University of Victoria in 1996 and his MPhil from Cambridge in 1998; by age 26 (1999) he was working as a freelance web designer. His first startup, Gradfinder.com, was built in 2000, and Flickr was not launched until 2004 when he was 31.
early_history_summary: Butterfield was born in Lund, British Columbia, and spent his first five years in a log cabin without running water or electricity on a commune. His family moved to Victoria when he was five. He taught himself programming at age seven on an Apple IIe. He earned a BA in philosophy from the University of Victoria (1996) and an MPhil from Clare College, Cambridge (1998). He worked as a web designer and built Gradfinder.com in 2000 before co-founding Ludicorp in 2002, which launched Flickr in 2004.
family_context_summary: Born in a remote fishing village in British Columbia; father fled the US to avoid the Vietnam draft and the family lived on a commune in a log cabin without running water or electricity for the first five years. Father later became a real estate developer. Family moved to Victoria, BC when Butterfield was five.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father became a real estate developer, which Butterfield says influenced his view of business cycles and fundraising, but no direct technology domain transfer documented.
evidence_summary: Butterfield taught himself programming at age seven and had early computer access, but pursued philosophy in university rather than computer science. His defining milestones came later: Flickr at 31 (2004) and Slack at 40 (2013). By age 26 he was a freelance web designer with a philosophy MPhil from Cambridge and no material career milestone.

name: Dries Buytaert
milestone_by_age_26: Released Drupal 1.0.0 as open-source software on January 15, 2001, at age 22; Drupal went on to become one of the world's most widely used content management systems, powering approximately 1 in 35 websites globally.
early_history_summary: Buytaert was born in Wilrijk, Antwerp, Belgium. He learned programming at age six on his father's Commodore 64, typing BASIC code from children's computer books before he could read. His father, a medical doctor, later asked him to build a patient management system, which deepened his programming skills. He studied computer science at the University of Antwerp starting in 1996, where he discovered Linux and contributed to open-source wireless network drivers. In 1999, at age 21, he built a message board for his dorm using PHP and MySQL, which evolved into drop.org and then Drupal, released as open source on January 15, 2001.
family_context_summary: Born in Antwerp, Belgium; father was a medical doctor with entrepreneurial inclinations who bought a Commodore 64 and later asked Dries to build a patient management system. Mother was caring and kind. One grandfather was a writer and publisher, the other a scientist who loved to invent. Middle-class family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a medical doctor who provided early computer access (Commodore 64 at age six) and gave Dries a real programming project (patient management system) using Clipper, which deepened his programming skills during a summer vacation. This provided early domain exposure to software development.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early computer access, father's programming project, open-source community, web frontier, self-taught programming
evidence_summary: Buytaert learned programming at age six on his father's Commodore 64 and built a patient management system for his father as a teenager, providing early domain exposure. At the University of Antwerp he discovered Linux and contributed to open-source projects. In 1999, at age 21, he built a dorm message board with PHP and MySQL that evolved into Drupal, released as open source on January 15, 2001, at age 22. His father, a medical doctor, provided the computer and a real-world programming task, but the Drupal project itself was self-initiated without institutional or investor support.
starting_point: Born in Wilrijk, Antwerp, Belgium to a medical doctor father and a caring mother; middle-class family with grandfather influences in writing/publishing and science/invention. Father provided early computer access.
current_position: Co-founder and Executive Chairman of Acquia (acquired by Vista Equity Partners for $1B in 2019); creator and project lead of Drupal, which powers approximately 1 in 35 websites globally; resides in Boston, Massachusetts.

trajectory.event: Released Drupal 1.0.0 as open-source software on January 15, 2001, from his University of Antwerp dorm project.
Co-founded Acquia with Jay Batson to provide commercial support and services for Drupal.
Named to MIT Technology Review TR35 as one of the top 35 innovators under 35; also named Young Entrepreneurs of Tech by BusinessWeek.
Defended PhD dissertation in computer science at Ghent University on profiling and instrumentation of the JVM.
Acquia helped re-launch Whitehouse.gov on Drupal, cementing Drupal's enterprise credibility.
Acquia acquired by Vista Equity Partners in a deal valuing the company at approximately $1 billion.
Transitioned to Executive Chairman of Acquia as Chris Tranquill was appointed CEO.

name: Rasmus Lerdorf
milestone_by_age_26: Released PHP 1.0 (Personal Home Page Tools) on June 8, 1995, at age 26, posting the announcement to the comp.infosystems.www.authoring.cgi Usenet newsgroup; PHP went on to become the most widely used server-side web programming language, powering over 76% of websites with a known server-side language.
early_history_summary: Lerdorf was born on Disko Island, Greenland, and moved to Denmark in his early years. His family moved to Canada in 1980 and to King City, Ontario in 1983. He graduated from King City Secondary School in 1988 and from the University of Waterloo in 1993 with a BASc in Systems Design Engineering, including co-op work terms at several companies. He started developing PHP tools in 1994 to solve practical web development problems, combining numerous small CGI programs into a unified C library and parser. He released PHP 1.0 on June 8, 1995.
family_context_summary: Born on Disko Island, Greenland; family moved to Denmark and then to Canada in 1980, settling in King City, Ontario in 1983. Family financial background not extensively documented; father's occupation not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family background in computer science or programming.
primary_early_advantage_tags: university of waterloo engineering, early web frontier, practical problem-solving, open-source community, self-taught web development
evidence_summary: Lerdorf grew up in Greenland, Denmark, and Canada, attending the University of Waterloo for Systems Design Engineering (1993). He developed PHP in 1994-1995 as a practical tool to solve his own web development problems, releasing version 1.0 on June 8, 1995, at age 26. He had no formal programming language design training and described himself as a pragmatic programmer. PHP's success came from solving real-world web problems at the dawn of the World Wide Web, riding the structural wave of web adoption. Family background is not well documented.
starting_point: Born on Disko Island, Greenland; family moved to Denmark and then to Canada in 1980, settling in King City, Ontario. Family background not extensively documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Distinguished Engineer at Etsy (joined 2012); creator of PHP, the most widely used server-side web programming language. Resides in the San Francisco Bay Area.

trajectory.event: Released PHP 1.0 (Personal Home Page Tools) on June 8, 1995, via a Usenet newsgroup announcement.
Contributed to the Apache HTTP Server project and added the LIMIT clause to the mSQL DBMS.
Joined Yahoo! Inc. as an Infrastructure Architecture Engineer, helping migrate Yahoo to PHP-based tools.
Named to MIT Technology Review's list of top innovators for creating PHP, which by then powered over 12 million websites.
Joined Etsy as Distinguished Engineer, working on architecture, internationalization, payments, fraud, and security.

He created Python as a side project during Christmas 1989, with the first public release (version 0.9.0) in February 1991.

name: Larry Wall
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Wall started at Seattle Pacific University in 1976 and graduated with a bachelor's degree in Natural and Artificial Languages; by age 26 (1980-1981) he was in graduate school at UC Berkeley studying linguistics. His first widely known software, rn (a Usenet newsreader), was written in 1984 at age 29-30, and Perl was released in 1987 at age 33.
early_history_summary: Wall grew up in Los Angeles and Bremerton, Washington. His father and grandfathers were pastors, and he planned to become a missionary. He started at Seattle Pacific University in 1976, majoring in chemistry and music, later pre-medicine, and eventually graduated with a degree in Natural and Artificial Languages (combining linguistics and computer science). He and his wife studied linguistics at UC Berkeley intending to create a writing system for an unwritten language, but health issues (food allergies) forced them to abandon missionary plans. Wall joined the NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory and later worked at System Development Corporation, where he developed Perl in 1987.

By age 26 he was a graduate student with no material career milestone.

He graduated from the University of Tsukuba with a degree in information science, where he was a member of Ikuo Nakata's research lab on programming languages and compilers. He worked at Network Communications Laboratory (Netlab.jp) and released cmail, an Emacs-based mail user agent. He released the first version of Ruby on December 21, 1995, at age 30.
